newsitem.title: ANTIGUA AND BARBUDA: CRICKET-LARA FINED FOR NOT ARRIVING ON TIME.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LARA FINED FOR NOT ARRIVING ON TIME.

text.p: Brian Lara has been fined by West Indies team management for failing to arrive here on time for last week's first test against Sri Lanka.
Lara, who had disciplinary problems at the World Cup early last year and on West indies tour of Australia later in the year, has been fined 50 percent of his match fee for the first test.
The West Indian players assembled in St. John's on Tuesday for the test starting on Friday, but Lara did not arrive until Wednesday night.
His explanation that he missed his flight was not accepted as a satisfactory excuse by the team's management.
For incidents at the World Cup, Lara had been reprimanded by West Indies Cricket Board's disciplinary committee and warned that any future acts of indiscipline would be dealt with strongly.

An outburst in Australia's dressing room last December after a controversial dismissal in the second test led to West Indies team management settling the issue "in house" and apologising to the Australians for Lara's action.
The West Indian board is reporting that this latest issue has been settled without affecting the team's morale, and the players are now focusing on the second and final test.
West Indies won the first test by six wickets.
